security_audit.summary: The skill is primarily a defensive security hardening workflow, but one validation step requests Metasploit, custom exploits, and proof-of-concept exploit output. The system-reconnaissance and jailbreak scanner hits are false positives because they refer to safety guidance and mobile root or jailbreak detection.

remediation.issue: Penetration testing prompt includes Metasploit and custom exploits.
remediation.suggestion: Limit validation to authorized environments and replace exploit execution with passive checks or controlled test plans.
Require sanitized reproduction steps and remediation evidence instead of exploit payloads or runnable attack instructions.

remediation.issue: Authorization guardrails are separate from the high-risk testing step.
remediation.suggestion: Place authorization, scope, rate-limit, and non-destructive testing requirements inside the penetration testing prompt.

finding_verdicts.reason: The prompt directs an agent to use Burp Suite, Metasploit, and custom exploits for penetration testing. Even with an authorization warning elsewhere, this enables offensive exploitation against arbitrary targets.
Line 31 is a safety limitation that warns against intrusive testing in production without approval. It does not instruct reconnaissance or exploitation.
Line 76 refers to root or jailbreak detection as a mobile hardening control. It is not a jailbreak prompt injection or bypass request.

content.value_statement: Security programs need coordinated scanning, remediation, and validation across many layers. This skill structures assessment, hardening, compliance, and monitoring work for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
actual_capabilities: Coordinates SAST, DAST, dependency, secrets, and SBOM assessment steps.
Guides STRIDE threat modeling and risk prioritization.
Plans remediation for OWASP Top 10, CVEs, authentication, and data protection issues.
Defines backend, frontend, mobile, infrastructure, and secrets hardening tasks.
Maps validation to OWASP ASVS, CIS, SOC2, GDPR, HIPAA, and PCI-DSS checks.
Outlines SIEM, alerting, and incident response monitoring integration.
limitations: Requires authorization and change approval before testing or hardening.
Does not execute tools by itself; it coordinates agent prompts and expected outputs.
May be unsafe for production unless test scope and rollback plans are defined.
Compliance output still needs review by qualified security and legal owners.

use_cases.title: Harden a Web Platform
use_cases.description: Application security teams can coordinate scans, fixes, and validation across web services and infrastructure.

use_cases.title: Prepare for Compliance Review
use_cases.description: Compliance teams can organize evidence and gap analysis against common security frameworks.

use_cases.title: Build DevSecOps Controls
use_cases.description: Platform teams can plan CI/CD scanning, secrets management, monitoring, and incident response coverage.

prompt_templates.title: Assess Security Baseline
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to assess the security baseline for my application. Focus on SAST, dependency scanning, secrets detection, and prioritized remediation.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Defense in Depth
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to create a defense-in-depth plan for my service. Include backend, frontend, infrastructure, secrets, and monitoring controls.

prompt_templates.title: Coordinate Remediation Program
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to organize remediation for high-risk findings. Prioritize by CVSS, exploitability, business impact, and required validation evidence.

prompt_templates.title: Validate Enterprise Security Posture
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to validate our security posture against OWASP ASVS, CIS, SOC2, and applicable privacy controls. Include monitoring gaps.

output_examples.input: A team asks for a first security baseline for a web API.
output: A scan plan covering SAST, dependency audit, secrets detection, and SBOM generation.
A prioritized remediation list with severity, ownership, and validation needs.
A summary of attack surface areas that need deeper review.

output_examples.input: A platform team needs hardening across cloud infrastructure and CI/CD.
output: A defense plan for network segmentation, IAM, secrets management, and CI/CD controls.
A rollback-aware implementation sequence for production-sensitive changes.
Monitoring and alerting requirements for security events.

output_examples.input: A compliance team needs evidence for SOC2 and OWASP ASVS.
output: A gap analysis mapped to requested frameworks.
A list of evidence artifacts needed from engineering and operations.
A remediation tracker for controls that fail validation.

best_practices: Confirm written authorization, scope, and test windows before running any security activity.
Start with non-destructive scans, then apply controlled remediation with rollback plans.
Review generated findings with security owners before changing production systems.
anti_patterns: Running intrusive tests against production systems without approval.
Requesting runnable exploit payloads when remediation evidence is enough.
Treating compliance checklists as proof of security without validation.

faq.question: Can this skill run security tools directly?
faq.answer: No. It provides coordinated prompts and expected outputs for supported AI tools.

faq.question: Is it safe for production systems?
faq.answer: Only with written authorization, scoped testing, and rollback plans.

faq.question: Which frameworks does it reference?
faq.answer: It references OWASP, CIS, SOC2, GDPR, HIPAA, and PCI-DSS.

faq.question: Does it replace a security engineer?
faq.answer: No. A qualified owner must review findings and approve changes.

faq.question: Can it support mobile apps?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes mobile hardening steps such as secure storage and root or jailbreak detection.

faq.question: Why was the audit strict?
faq.answer: One step requests Metasploit, custom exploits, and proof-of-concept exploit output.
